phrases.arabic: فِي أَيِّ سَاعَةٍ يَجِبُ أَنْ أُغَادِرَ الْفُنْدُق؟
phrases.transliteration: fii ayyi saa3atin yajibu an ughaadira al-funduq?

reply.english: You're welcome, we wish you a pleasant stay.

dialogue.speaker: Guest
dialogue.english: Hello, I have a reservation.

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.english: Welcome, under whose name?

dialogue.speaker: Guest
dialogue.english: Under the name Nour.

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.english: Yes, a room for two people for three nights.

dialogue.speaker: Guest
dialogue.english: Is breakfast included with the room?

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.english: Yes, from seven until nine.

dialogue.speaker: Guest
dialogue.english: Can I see the room first?

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.english: Of course. Here is the key.

dialogue.speaker: Guest
dialogue.english: Where is the elevator?

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.english: On your right after the door.

dialogue.speaker: Guest
dialogue.arabic: فِي أَيِّ سَاعَةٍ يَجِبُ أَنْ أُغَادِرَ؟
dialogue.transliteration: fii ayyi saa3atin yajibu an ughaadira?
dialogue.english: What time do I need to check out?

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.english: Before twelve noon.

lessons.culture: At a hotel reception in any Arab country, staff speak Fusha or a mix with the local dialect, and a polite مِنْ فَضْلِك goes a long way. Breakfast is often included, and check-out is usually around noon.

phrases.arabic: هَلْ يُوجَدُ مَقْعَدٌ شَاغِرٌ فِي الْحَافِلَةِ الْقَادِمَة؟
phrases.transliteration: hal yoojadu maq3adun shaaghirun fii al-7aafilati al-qaadima?

reply.english: You're welcome, have a good trip.

dialogue.speaker: Passenger
dialogue.english: Hello, I want to book a bus ticket.

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.english: Welcome. To where?

dialogue.speaker: Passenger
dialogue.english: Do you have tickets to Aleppo?

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، مُتَوَفِّرَة. هَلْ تُرِيدُ ذَهَابًا وَإِيَابًا؟
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, mutawaffira. hal tureedu dhahaaban wa iyaaban?
dialogue.english: Yes, available. Do you want a round trip?

dialogue.speaker: Passenger
dialogue.english: No, I want a one-way ticket only.

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.arabic: يُوجَدُ مَقْعَدٌ شَاغِرٌ فِي الْحَافِلَةِ الْقَادِمَة.
dialogue.transliteration: yoojadu maq3adun shaaghirun fii al-7aafilati al-qaadima.
dialogue.english: There is a free seat on the next bus.

dialogue.speaker: Passenger
dialogue.english: What time does it leave?

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.english: At eight in the morning.

dialogue.speaker: Passenger
dialogue.english: Can I pay by card?

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.english: Yes, here is your ticket.

dialogue.speaker: Passenger
dialogue.english: Thanks. How long does the trip take?

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.english: About five hours. Have a good trip.

pair.english: Do you have tickets to Aleppo?
What time does the bus leave?
How long does the trip take?

lessons.culture: Intercity buses and coaches are the usual way to travel between Arab cities, and tickets are bought at the ticket window or online. Students often get a discount if they show a card, so asking is normal.

reply.english: At the end of the hall.

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.english: Where is the check-in counter?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.arabic: فِي آخِرِ الْقَاعَة. جَوَازُ السَّفَرِ مِنْ فَضْلِك.
dialogue.transliteration: fii aakhiri al-qaa3a. jawaazu as-safari min fadlik.
dialogue.english: At the end of the hall. Your passport please.

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.english: I have my passport and my ticket.

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.english: How many bags am I allowed to take?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.arabic: حَقِيبَتَانِ. هَلْ هَذِهِ الْحَقِيبَةُ زَائِدَةُ الْوَزْن؟
dialogue.english: Two bags. Is this bag overweight?

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.english: I don't think so. Where is the boarding gate?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.arabic: الْبَوَّابَةُ الثَّالِثَة. تُقْلِعُ الطَّائِرَةُ فِي الْعَاشِرَة.
dialogue.transliteration: al-bawwaabatu ath-thaalitha. tuqli3u at-taa2iratu fii al-3aashira.
dialogue.english: Gate three. The plane departs at ten.

dialogue.speaker: Officer
dialogue.arabic: جَوَازُ السَّفَرِ مِنْ فَضْلِك. هَلْ أَتَيْتَ لِلسِّيَاحَةِ أَمْ لِلْعَمَل؟
dialogue.transliteration: jawaazu as-safari min fadlik. hal ataita lis-siyaa7ati am lil-3amal?
dialogue.english: Your passport please. Are you coming for tourism or work?

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.english: For tourism.

dialogue.speaker: Officer
dialogue.english: How long will you stay here?

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.english: Two weeks.

dialogue.speaker: Officer
dialogue.english: Do you have anything to declare?

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.english: No, I don't have anything.

dialogue.speaker: Officer
dialogue.english: Welcome.

pair.english: Do you have anything to declare?
Are you coming for tourism or work?
How long will you stay here?

lessons.culture: At the airport the border officer usually asks short questions in Fusha or the local dialect: purpose of the visit, length of stay, anything to declare. A calm, polite answer and a greeting like أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا from the officer mark a smooth arrival.

phrases.arabic: عَوَّضَ اللهُ عَلَيْكَ، إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ تُحَلُّ الْمُشْكِلَة
phrases.transliteration: 3awwada allaahu 3alayka, in shaa2a allaahu tu7allu al-mushkila

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.english: Excuse me, I lost my bag.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.english: Certainly, what happened?

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.arabic: لَمْ أَجِدْهَا بَعْدَ الرِّحْلَة، وَتَكَسَّرَتْ حَقِيبَتِي الْأُخْرَى.
dialogue.transliteration: lam ajidhaa ba3da ar-ri7la, wa takassarat 7aqeebatee al-ukhraa.
dialogue.english: I couldn't find it after the flight, and my other bag got broken.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.arabic: أَيْنَ مَكْتَبُ الشَّكَاوَى؟ هُوَ عَلَى يَسَارِكَ.
dialogue.english: The complaints office? It is on your left.

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.english: Thanks. The plane is also very delayed.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.english: I apologise. Do you have another booking?

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.arabic: هُنَاكَ مُشْكِلَةٌ فِي الْحَجْز. فَاتَتْنِي الرِّحْلَة، مَاذَا أَفْعَل؟
dialogue.transliteration: hunaaka mushkilatun fii al-7ajz. faatatnee ar-ri7la, maadha af3al?
dialogue.english: There's a problem with the booking. I missed the flight, what do I do?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.arabic: تَحْتَاجُ إِلَى تَغْيِيرِ الرِّحْلَة. تَعَالَ مَعِي.
dialogue.transliteration: ta7taaju ilaa taghyeeri ar-ri7la. ta3aala ma3ee.
dialogue.english: You need to change the flight. Come with me.

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.english: Nobody answered me a moment ago.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.english: I apologise again. We will help you now.

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.english: Thank you.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.arabic: عَوَّضَ اللهُ عَلَيْكَ، إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ تُحَلُّ الْمُشْكِلَة.
dialogue.transliteration: 3awwada allaahu 3alayka, in shaa2a allaahu tu7allu al-mushkila.
dialogue.english: May God make up for it, God willing the problem will be solved.

pair.english: I missed the flight, what do I do?

response.english: You need to change the flight.

lessons.culture: When something goes wrong while travelling, people ask for help politely with مِنْ فَضْلِك and explain the problem in a short sentence. A common thing to say to someone facing a setback is عَوَّضَ اللهُ عَلَيْكَ, and the usual answer is آمِين.

reply.arabic: مِنَ التَّاسِعَةِ صَبَاحًا حَتَّى الْخَامِسَةِ مَسَاءً
reply.transliteration: min at-taasi3ati SabaaHan Hattaa al-khaamisati masaa2an
reply.english: From nine in the morning until five in the evening.
Yes, it is one of the most beautiful sights.

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.arabic: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. أَيْنَ الْمَتْحَفُ الْوَطَنِيّ مِنْ فَضْلِك؟
dialogue.transliteration: as-salaamu 3alaykum. ayna al-matHafu al-waTaniyy min faDlik?
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you. Where is the national museum, please?

dialogue.speaker: Passerby
dialogue.arabic: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَام. اِمْشِي مُبَاشَرَةً ثُمَّ اِنْعَطِفِي يَسَارًا.
dialogue.transliteration: wa 3alaykumu as-salaam. imshee mubaashiratan thumma in3aTifee yasaaran.
dialogue.english: And peace be upon you. Walk straight, then turn left.

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.english: Thank you very much. Is it far?

dialogue.speaker: Passerby
dialogue.arabic: لَا، خَمْسُ دَقَائِقَ سَيْرًا عَلَى الْأَقْدَام.
dialogue.english: No, five minutes on foot.

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.english: Hello, how much is the entry ticket?

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.english: Ten for an adult and five for a child.

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.arabic: تَذْكِرَتَانِ مِنْ فَضْلِك. وَمَا هِيَ مَوَاعِيدُ الْفَتْح؟
dialogue.transliteration: tadhkiratani min faDlik. wa maa hiya mawaa3eedu al-fatH?
dialogue.english: Two tickets, please. And what are the opening hours?

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.arabic: مِنَ التَّاسِعَةِ صَبَاحًا حَتَّى الْخَامِسَةِ مَسَاءً، وَهُوَ مُغْلَقٌ يَوْمَ الْإِثْنَيْن.
dialogue.transliteration: min at-taasi3ati SabaaHan Hattaa al-khaamisati masaa2an, wa huwa mughlaqun yawma al-ithnayn.
dialogue.english: From nine in the morning until five in the evening, and it is closed on Monday.

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.english: Can I take photos inside the halls?

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.english: Yes, but without the flash.

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.arabic: وَأَيْنَ الْمَسْجِدُ الْكَبِير؟ أُرِيدُ زِيَارَتَهُ بَعْدَ الْمَتْحَف.
dialogue.transliteration: wa ayna al-masjidu al-kabeer? ureedu ziyaaratahu ba3da al-matHaf.
dialogue.english: And where is the grand mosque? I want to visit it after the museum.

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.arabic: هُوَ قَرِيبٌ مِنْ هُنَا. وَيُرْجَى خَلْعُ الْحِذَاءِ عِنْدَ الْمَدْخَل.
dialogue.transliteration: huwa qareebun min hunaa. wa yurjaa khal3u al-Hidhaa2i 3inda al-madkhal.
dialogue.english: It is close to here. And please take off your shoes at the entrance.

response.arabic: مِنَ التَّاسِعَةِ صَبَاحًا حَتَّى الْخَامِسَةِ مَسَاءً
response.transliteration: min at-taasi3ati SabaaHan Hattaa al-khaamisati masaa2an
response.english: From nine in the morning until five in the evening.
Yes, it is one of the most beautiful sights.

lessons.culture: Mosques are open to visitors outside prayer times in many places. Visitors take off their shoes at the entrance, dress modestly and speak quietly, and women usually cover their hair. Museums and old cities are often closed one day a week, so ask يَوْمَ الْإِغْلَاق (the closing day) before you go.

exercises.tip: murshid is a guide; jawla is a tour.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'Where is the national museum?'
exercises.tip: ayna opens the question, then the noun.

exercises.prompt: Which one means 'What are the opening hours?'
exercises.tip: mawaa3eed are times; al-fatH is the opening.

exercises.prompt: Which one means 'Please take off your shoes at the entrance'?
exercises.tip: Said at the door of a mosque.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'How much is the entry ticket?'
exercises.tip: bikam asks the price and comes first.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'Walk straight, then turn left'
exercises.tip: thumma means then. To a woman: imshee ... in3aTifee.

exercises.tip: at-taSweer is photographing.

exercises.tip: qadeem is old; it agrees with madeena, which is feminine.

exercises.answer: مِنَ التَّاسِعَةِ صَبَاحًا حَتَّى الْخَامِسَةِ مَسَاءً
accepted: مِنَ التَّاسِعَةِ صَبَاحًا حَتَّى الْخَامِسَةِ مَسَاءً
من التاسعة صباحا حتى الخامسة مساء
min at-taasi3ati SabaaHan Hattaa al-khaamisati masaa2an
exercises.tip: min ... Hattaa means from ... until.

exercises.prompt: You hear: 'مَا أَجْمَلَ هَذَا الْمَكَان!'. Agree.
exercises.tip: ma3aalim are landmarks or sights.

phrases.arabic: هَلْ مَعَكَ كِرِيمٌ وَاقٍ مِنَ الشَّمْس؟
phrases.transliteration: hal ma3aka kreemun waaqin mina ash-shams?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: The sea is beautiful today, Huda!

dialogue.speaker: Huda
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، وَلَكِنَّ الْجَوَّ حَارٌّ جِدًّا. أَيْنَ نَجْلِسُ؟
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, wa lakinna al-jawwa Haarrun jiddan. ayna najlisu?
dialogue.english: Yes, but the weather is very hot. Where do we sit?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: لِنَسْتَأْجِرْ مِظَلَّةَ شَاطِئٍ قَرِيبَةً مِنَ الْمَاء.
dialogue.transliteration: li-nasta2jir miDallata shaaTi2in qareebatan mina al-maa2.
dialogue.english: Let us rent a beach umbrella near the water.

dialogue.speaker: Huda
dialogue.arabic: هَلْ مَعَكَ كِرِيمٌ وَاقٍ مِنَ الشَّمْسِ لِلْأَطْفَال؟
dialogue.transliteration: hal ma3aka kreemun waaqin mina ash-shamsi lil-aTfaal?
dialogue.english: Do you have sunscreen for the children?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، مَعِي. هَيَّا يَا أَطْفَال، ضَعُوا الْكِرِيمَ أَوَّلًا.
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, ma3ee. hayyaa yaa aTfaal, Da3oo al-kreema awwalan.
dialogue.english: Yes, I have it. Come on, children, put the cream on first.

dialogue.speaker: Huda
dialogue.arabic: أَيْنَ مُنْقِذُ الْغَرْقَى؟ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَسْأَلَهُ.
dialogue.transliteration: ayna munqidhu al-gharqaa? ureedu an as2alahu.
dialogue.english: Where is the lifeguard? I want to ask him.

dialogue.speaker: Lifeguard
dialogue.arabic: أَنَا هُنَا يَا سَيِّدَتِي. كَيْفَ أُسَاعِدُكِ؟
dialogue.transliteration: ana hunaa yaa sayyidatee. kayfa usaa3iduki?
dialogue.english: I am here, madam. How can I help you?

dialogue.speaker: Huda
dialogue.english: Is swimming safe here today?

dialogue.speaker: Lifeguard
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، لَكِنَّ الْأَمْوَاجَ عَالِيَةٌ قَلِيلًا، فَلَا تَبْتَعِدُوا عَنِ الشَّاطِئ.
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, lakinna al-amwaaja 3aaliyatun qaleelan, falaa tabta3idoo 3ani ash-shaaTi2.
dialogue.english: Yes, but the waves are a little high, so do not go far from the shore.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: حَاضِر، شُكْرًا لَكَ. هَلِ الْمَاءُ بَارِد؟
dialogue.transliteration: HaaDir, shukran laka. hal al-maa2u baarid?
dialogue.english: Understood, thank you. Is the water cold?

dialogue.speaker: Lifeguard
dialogue.transliteration: laa, daafi2un wa munaasib. istamti3oo biwaqtikum!
dialogue.english: No, it is warm and just right. Enjoy your time!

dialogue.speaker: Huda
dialogue.arabic: بَارَكَ اللهُ فِيكَ. هَيَّا لِنَبْنِيَ قَلْعَةً مِنَ الرَّمْلِ مَعَ الْأَطْفَال!
dialogue.transliteration: baaraka allaahu feeka. hayyaa li-nabniya qal3atan mina ar-raml ma3a al-aTfaal!
dialogue.english: God bless you. Come on, let us build a sandcastle with the children!

response.english: No, it is warm and just right.

pair.english: Is it safe to swim here?

response.english: Yes, but watch out for the waves.

pair.arabic: هَلْ مَعَكَ كِرِيمٌ وَاقٍ مِنَ الشَّمْس؟
pair.transliteration: hal ma3aka kreemun waaqin mina ash-shams?

lessons.culture: Families usually go to a family beach and wear modest swimwear, and many keep out of the midday sun and bring plenty of water. Swim near the lifeguard and obey the flag colours, because sea conditions in summer can change quickly.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'I want to swim'
exercises.tip: an asbaHa: the verb after an is in the subjunctive.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'Is it safe to swim here?'
exercises.tip: as-sibaaHa is swimming as a noun; aamina is safe.

exercises.prompt: Which one means 'The waves are high today'?
exercises.tip: amwaaj is waves; 3aaliya is high.

exercises.prompt: Which one means 'Do you have sunscreen?'
options: هَلْ مَعَكَ كِرِيمٌ وَاقٍ مِنَ الشَّمْس؟
exercises.answer: هَلْ مَعَكَ كِرِيمٌ وَاقٍ مِنَ الشَّمْس؟
accepted: هَلْ مَعَكَ كِرِيمٌ وَاقٍ مِنَ الشَّمْس؟

exercises.tip: waaqin mina ash-shams: protecting from the sun.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'Where is the lifeguard?'
exercises.tip: munqidh is a rescuer; al-gharqaa are the drowning.

exercises.tip: miDalla is an umbrella; shaaTi2 is the beach.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'الْأَطْفَالُ يَبْنُونَ قَلْعَةً مِنَ _____' (The children are building a sandcastle from sand)
exercises.tip: raml is sand; qal3a is a castle.

exercises.prompt: You hear: 'هَلِ الْمَاءُ بَارِد؟'. Say it is warm and just right.
exercises.tip: daafi2 is warm.

exercises.prompt: You are the lifeguard and hear: 'هَلِ السِّبَاحَةُ آمِنَةٌ هُنَا؟'. Say yes, but watch out for the waves.
exercises.tip: intabih is a command: be careful.

reply.english: I have many things, please look.

phrases.arabic: أُرِيدُ زُجَاجَةً صَغِيرَةً مِنْ دُهْنِ الْعُودِ
phrases.transliteration: ureedu zujaajatan Saghiratan min duhni al-3oud

reply.english: Yes, it was made by hand.

phrases.arabic: هَلْ تُعْطِينِي سِعْرًا أَقَلَّ إِذَا اشْتَرَيْتُ اثْنَيْنِ؟
phrases.transliteration: hal tu3Teenee si3ran aqalla idhaa ishtaraytu ithnayn?

reply.english: All right, you get a small discount.

phrases.arabic: هَذِهِ هَدِيَّةٌ لِأُمِّي، أَتَمَنَّى أَنْ تُعْجِبَهَا
phrases.transliteration: haadhihi hadiyyatun li-ummee, atamannaa an tu3jibahaa

reply.english: God willing she will like it.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ، أُرِيدُ هَدِيَّةً تِذْكَارِيَّةً لِأُسْرَتِي.
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you, I want a souvenir for my family.

dialogue.speaker: Abu Khaled
dialogue.arabic: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ، أَهْلًا بِكَ. عِنْدِي أَشْيَاءُ كَثِيرَةٌ، تَفَضَّلْ.
dialogue.transliteration: wa 3alaykumu as-salaam, ahlan bika. 3indee ashyaa2u katheeratun, tafaDDal.
dialogue.english: And peace be upon you, welcome. I have many things, please look.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: Do you have good dates?

dialogue.speaker: Abu Khaled
dialogue.english: Yes, please taste some.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: طَيِّبٌ جِدًّا، سَآخُذُ عُلْبَةً. وَمَا هَذَا الْعِطْرُ؟
dialogue.transliteration: Tayyibun jiddan, sa-aakhudhu 3ulbatan. wa maa haadhaa al-3iTr?
dialogue.english: Very tasty, I will take a box. And what is this perfume?

dialogue.speaker: Abu Khaled
dialogue.english: This is natural oud, and its scent is lovely.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: Is this box handmade?

dialogue.speaker: Abu Khaled
dialogue.english: Yes, it was made by hand.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: أُرِيدُ سَجَّادَةَ صَلَاةٍ أَيْضًا. هَلْ تُعْطِينِي سِعْرًا أَقَلَّ إِذَا اشْتَرَيْتُ اثْنَيْنِ؟
dialogue.transliteration: ureedu sajjaadata Salaatin aydan. hal tu3Teenee si3ran aqalla idhaa ishtaraytu ithnayn?
dialogue.english: I want a prayer rug too. Will you give me a lower price if I buy two?

dialogue.speaker: Abu Khaled
dialogue.english: All right, you get a small discount.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: Can you wrap it as a gift?

dialogue.speaker: Abu Khaled
dialogue.english: With pleasure, God bless you.

response.english: Yes, it was made by hand.

pair.arabic: هَلْ تُعْطِينِي سِعْرًا أَقَلَّ إِذَا اشْتَرَيْتُ اثْنَيْنِ؟
pair.transliteration: hal tu3Teenee si3ran aqalla idhaa ishtaraytu ithnayn?
pair.english: Will you give me a lower price if I buy two?

response.english: All right, you get a small discount.

lessons.culture: Dates, oud and a prayer rug are the classic gifts carried home from a trip, and a gift is chosen for each person by name. Bargaining is gentle: ask for a better price once, politely, and a seller often offers a taste or a small discount in return.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'I want a prayer rug'
exercises.tip: sajjaada is a rug; Salaah is the prayer.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'Is this handmade?'
exercises.tip: yadawiyyan means by hand.

exercises.tip: maSnoo3 means made.

exercises.answer: هَلْ تُعْطِينِي سِعْرًا أَقَلَّ إِذَا اشْتَرَيْتُ اثْنَيْنِ؟
accepted: هَلْ تُعْطِينِي سِعْرًا أَقَلَّ إِذَا اشْتَرَيْتُ اثْنَيْنِ؟
هل تعطيني سعرا أقل إذا اشتريت اثنين؟
hal tu3Teenee si3ran aqalla idhaa ishtaraytu ithnayn?
exercises.tip: Ask once and politely; buying two gives you a reason.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'Can you wrap it as a gift?'
exercises.tip: ka- before hadiyya means as a gift.

exercises.answer: أُرِيدُ زُجَاجَةً صَغِيرَةً مِنْ دُهْنِ الْعُودِ
accepted: أُرِيدُ زُجَاجَةً صَغِيرَةً مِنْ دُهْنِ الْعُودِ
أريد زجاجة صغيرة من دهن العود
ureedu zujaajatan Saghiratan min duhni al-3oud
exercises.tip: The thing comes first, then its small size, then min and what it holds.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'هَلْ عِنْدَكَ _____ جَيِّدٌ؟' (Do you have good dates?)
exercises.tip: tamr is dates; jayyid is good.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'أُرِيدُ وِشَاحًا _____ لِأُخْتِي' (I want a silk scarf for my sister)
exercises.tip: The describing word follows the scarf and takes -an too.

exercises.tip: Praise the taste, then say what you will take.

exercises.prompt: You ask: 'هَلْ هَذَا مَصْنُوعٌ يَدَوِيًّا؟'. The seller answers. What does he say?
exercises.tip: Suni3a is the passive: it was made.

reply.english: I will travel to the sea.

phrases.arabic: هَلْ تَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ تَلْتَقِطَ لَنَا صُورَةً؟
phrases.transliteration: hal tastaTee3u an taltaqiTa lanaa Sooratan?

reply.english: Right away, I will send them now.
It was wonderful and we enjoyed it a lot.
Welcome back, thank God for your safety.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: إِلَى أَيْنَ سَتَذْهَبُونَ فِي الْعُطْلَةِ يَا رَنَا؟
dialogue.transliteration: ilaa ayna sa-tadhhaboona fee al-3uTlati yaa rana?
dialogue.english: Where are you going this holiday, Rana?

dialogue.speaker: Rana
dialogue.arabic: سَنُسَافِرُ إِلَى الْبَحْرِ مَعَ الْعَائِلَةِ كُلِّهَا.
dialogue.transliteration: sa-nusaafiru ilaa al-baHri ma3a al-3aa2ilati kullihaa.
dialogue.english: We will travel to the sea with the whole family.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: How long does your holiday last?

dialogue.speaker: Rana
dialogue.arabic: تَدُومُ أُسْبُوعَيْنِ. حَجَزْنَا بَيْتًا قُرْبَ الشَّاطِئِ.
dialogue.transliteration: tadoomu usboo3ayn. Hajaznaa baytan qurba ash-shaaTi2.
dialogue.english: Two weeks. We booked a house near the beach.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Wonderful! Will you take your camera with you?

dialogue.speaker: Rana
dialogue.english: Of course, and I will send you the photos.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ عَلَى السَّلَامَةِ يَا رَنَا! كَيْفَ كَانَتْ رِحْلَتُكُمْ؟
dialogue.transliteration: al-Hamdu lillaahi 3alaa as-salaama yaa rana! kayfa kaanat riHlatukum?
dialogue.english: Welcome back, Rana! How was your trip? (after the holiday)

dialogue.speaker: Rana
dialogue.arabic: كَانَتْ رَائِعَةً وَاسْتَمْتَعْنَا كَثِيرًا، وَعُدْنَا سَالِمِينَ.
dialogue.transliteration: kaanat raa2i3atan wa istamta3naa katheeran, wa 3udnaa saalimeen.
dialogue.english: It was wonderful, we enjoyed it a lot, and we came back safe.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Do you have photos?

dialogue.speaker: Rana
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، انْظُرْ، مَا أَجْمَلَ هَذَا الْمَنْظَرَ!
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, unZur, maa ajmala haadhaa al-manZar!
dialogue.english: Yes, look, what a beautiful view!

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: فِعْلًا جَمِيلٌ. أَرْسِلِي لِي الصُّوَرَ عَلَى الْهَاتِفِ.
dialogue.transliteration: fi3lan jameel. arsilee lee aS-Suwara 3alaa al-haatif.
dialogue.english: Truly beautiful. Send me the photos on my phone.

dialogue.speaker: Rana
dialogue.english: Right away, I will send them now.

pair.english: Where are you going this holiday?

response.english: I will travel to the sea.
It was wonderful and we enjoyed it a lot.

pair.arabic: هَلْ تَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ تَلْتَقِطَ لَنَا صُورَةً؟
pair.transliteration: hal tastaTee3u an taltaqiTa lanaa Sooratan?
pair.english: Can you take a photo of us?
We came back safe, thank God.

response.english: Welcome back, thank God for your safety.

lessons.culture: Holiday plans are shared openly with friends and family, and a person back from a trip is greeted with al-Hamdu lillaahi 3alaa as-salaama, thanks to God for a safe return. Asking a passer-by to take a photo of the group is polite and common; photographing strangers without asking is not.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'Can you take a photo of us?'
exercises.answer: هَلْ تَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ تَلْتَقِطَ لَنَا صُورَةً؟
accepted: هَلْ تَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ تَلْتَقِطَ لَنَا صُورَةً؟
هل تستطيع أن تلتقط لنا صورة؟
hal tastaTee3u an taltaqiTa lanaa Sooratan?
exercises.tip: taltaqiTa means take, lanaa means for us.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'What a beautiful view!'
exercises.tip: maa ajmala plus a noun means how beautiful is...

exercises.prompt: Which one do you say to welcome someone back from a trip?
exercises.tip: It thanks God for the traveller's safety.

exercises.prompt: Which one asks 'Where are you going this holiday?'
exercises.tip: ilaa ayna is to where.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'We booked a house near the beach'
exercises.tip: The verb comes first; qurba is near.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'How was your trip?'
exercises.tip: kaanat is feminine because riHla is feminine.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'إِلَى أَيْنَ سَتَذْهَبُ فِي _____؟' (Where are you going this holiday?)
exercises.tip: fee takes the -i ending: al-3uTlati.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'أَرْسِلْ لِي _____ عَلَى الْهَاتِفِ' (Send me the photos on my phone)
exercises.tip: Suwar is the plural of Soora, photo.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks: 'كَيْفَ كَانَتْ رِحْلَتُكَ؟'. Answer that it was wonderful.
exercises.tip: Say it was wonderful and that you enjoyed it.

exercises.prompt: A friend says: 'عُدْنَا سَالِمِينَ، الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ'. Reply naturally.
exercises.tip: The set reply to someone back from a trip.

challenge.title: A trip from start to finish
challenge.instructions: Write a short conversation in Fusha in which you book a ticket, check in at a hotel, ask about breakfast and check-out, and report a lost bag politely.
required_elements: a request for a ticket with the price asked
a hotel reservation under a name
a question about breakfast or check-out time
a problem explained with فَقَدْتُ or فَاتَتْنِي
a polite request with مِنْ فَضْلِك and thanks

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: مِنْ فَضْلِك، أُرِيدُ تَذْكِرَةَ ذَهَابٍ وَإِيَابٍ إِلَى حَلَب.
dialogue.transliteration: min fadlik, ureedu tadhkirata dhahaabin wa iyaabin ilaa 7alab.
dialogue.english: Please, I want a round-trip ticket to Aleppo.

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.arabic: تَفَضَّلْ. كَمْ سِعْرُ التَّذْكِرَة؟ مِئَةُ دُولَار.
dialogue.transliteration: tafaddal. kam si3ru at-tadhkira? mi2atu doolaar.
dialogue.english: Here you are. The ticket price? One hundred dollars.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: شُكْرًا. عِنْدِي حَجْزٌ فِي الْفُنْدُقِ بِاسْمِ يُوسُف.
dialogue.english: Thanks. I have a hotel booking under the name Yusuf.

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.english: Welcome. Here is the key.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Is breakfast included with the room?

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، وَيَجِبُ أَنْ تُغَادِرَ قَبْلَ الظُّهْر.
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, wa yajibu an tughaadira qabla az-zuhr.
dialogue.english: Yes, and you need to check out before noon.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: فَقَدْتُ حَقِيبَتِي فِي الْمَطَار. أَيْنَ مَكْتَبُ الشَّكَاوَى؟
dialogue.transliteration: faqadtu 7aqeebatee fii al-mataar. ayna maktabu ash-shakaawaa?
dialogue.english: I lost my bag at the airport. Where is the complaints office?

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.english: We will help you. May God make up for it.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Amen. Thank you very much.

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.english: You're welcome. A pleasant stay.
